# Design a sales org's structure by stage: topology, ratios, spans, transitions

Curated by Skill Harbor — Maya-Beth Finotti's sales org-design skill: a structural design exercise for a VP Sales, CRO or founder scaling past founder-led selling, for B2B and B2C. The method: run the interview first (what triggered this, motion, deal size, current shape, behavioral signals, segments, expansion ownership, attrition/ramp, hiring plan, deadline, mandate, effort ceiling), then pick from a structural-move menu ranked by efficiency — frontline manager, SDR split, hunter/farmer split, segment pods — where every move fires only on its behavioral trigger (a hard rule: no move without a fired trigger is designed). Topologies are stage-gated, not substitutes: island (1-5 reps), assembly line (B2B SaaS, roughly $10M-$200M ARR), pod (~20+ reps, complex enterprise), hybrid where mature orgs actually land. The SDR:AE ratio is DERIVED from the org's own funnel math — never copied from a published number, with honest handling of contested figures. Spans set by role (median 7 AEs per manager), expansion ownership with the credited-tail rule, a written transition plan, next-stage triggers, and a measurement gate that must pass 100% before the design is done. Includes the B2B vs B2C deltas (published benchmarks are B2B SaaS data; commission-agent verticals and retail/call-center structures differ fundamentally) and failure modes (specializing too early/late, copying published ratios, pods as default upgrade, restructuring on the calendar).
